# `scikitplot.annoy`

<!-- Generated by `python tools/maint_tools/generate_usage_skills.py sync` from the installed package; edit the module's docstrings or `__all__`, not this file. -->

Public Annoy Python API for scikitplot.

## Install

```sh
pip install scikit-plots
pip install scikit-plots-annoy  # this part only
```

## Public API

Declared in `scikitplot.annoy.__all__`, in that order.

| Name | Kind | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `Annoy` | class | Compiled with GCC/Clang. |
| `AnnoyIndex` | class | Compiled with GCC/Clang. |
| `CompressMode` | type alias |  |
| `Index` | class | High-level ANNoy index composed from mixins. |
| `IndexIOMixin` | class | Mixin adding explicit Annoy-native persistence helpers. |
| `MetaMixin` | class | Mixin that exports and restores index metadata. |
| `NDArrayMixin` | class | NumPy / SciPy / pandas interoperability for Annoy-like indexes. |
| `PickleMixin` | class | Mixin adding pickle support. |
| `PickleMode` | type alias |  |
| `PlottingMixin` | class | Mixin that adds convenient plotting methods to high-level Annoy wrappers. |
| `VectorOpsMixin` | class | User-facing neighbor queries for Annoy-like backends. |
| `threads_info` | function | Describe what decides the number of threads in this process. |

All names with signatures: [references/API.md](references/API.md).

## Example (from the docstring of `scikitplot.annoy`)

```pycon
>>> import random
>>> random.seed(0)

>>> # from annoy import AnnoyIndex
>>> from scikitplot.cexternals._annoy import Annoy, AnnoyIndex
>>> from scikitplot.annoy import Annoy, AnnoyIndex, Index

>>> f = 40  # vector dimensionality
>>> t = Index(f, "angular")  # same constructor as the low-level backend
>>> t.add_item(0, [1] * f)
>>> t.build(10)  # Build 10 trees
>>> t.get_nns_by_item(0, 1)  # Find nearest neighbor
```
